problem_statement: This is an Astro learning-blog built on the withastro blog tutorial demo: a home page, an About page, a Blog index that lists tutorial posts, individual post pages, and tag routes (a Tags index plus per-tag pages), all under a shared Header/Footer with a light/dark theme toggle and a mobile menu. The editor wants a small, consistent 'Reading room' panel to sit in the footer of every reading surface: a labelled row of the blog's topic chips (Astro, Blogging, Community, Learning in public, Successes) plus a live 'Room light' readout that tells the reader whether the page is currently set for daylight (light theme) or lamplight (dark theme) — a reader adjusts a reading lamp for day versus night, so the panel should always name the lighting the page is set to. Ship the Reading room so it (1) appears in the footer on the home, blog, About and tag pages alike, (2) lays out its chip row responsively without horizontal overflow on a phone, (3) matches the blog's quiet ivory/indigo editorial styling (dashed accent chips keyed to the palette) rather than an off-palette slab, and (4) keeps the 'Room light' readout in sync with the theme toggle so a reader who switches to dark sees the readout update to lamplight. Keep the rest of the site — navigation, existing posts and tag routing, the mobile menu, RSS and the Astro build — intact with no console or network errors.
required_content: Add a shared 'Reading room' strip to the site footer so it renders on the home, blog, About and tag pages (a shared component invoked from Footer.astro, not a per-page copy).
The strip shows a 'From the reading room' label, a chip row of the blog's topic tags (Astro, Blogging, Community, Learning in public, Successes), and a 'Room light' readout.
The chip row must wrap responsively so no reading surface overflows horizontally on a 390px phone (overflow tolerance 24px).
Style the strip in the blog's quiet ivory/indigo editorial language (dashed accent chips keyed to the palette), consistent across light and dark, not an off-palette dark slab.

Wire the 'Room light' readout to the existing theme toggle: after clicking the theme button, the readout must read 'lamplight' in dark and 'daylight' in light — it must re-read the live theme, not show a stale captured value.
Preserve navigation (Home/About/Blog/Tags), the footer, the existing post/tag content, the mobile menu, light/dark theming and the Astro build with no console or network errors.
design_constraints: Implement the Reading room as a shared component rendered from the footer so a single source of truth reaches every page; do not paste divergent copies per page or build a detached widget.
The chip row must use a fluid, wrapping layout (no fixed-width nowrap track) so it never forces horizontal overflow on tablet or mobile.
The strip must adopt the blog's ivory/indigo palette and a dashed-tag idiom so it reads as part of the site, not a foreign block.
The 'Room light' readout must reflect the CURRENT theme after every toggle by reading the live theme class, so it can never go stale relative to the visible theme.
Do not remove or regress the navigation, existing content, tag routing, the mobile menu, RSS or the Astro build.
state_constraints: desktop_initial and mobile_initial protect the homepage and responsive shell.

desktop_blog_flow, tablet_blog_flow, mobile_blog_flow, desktop_tag_index, desktop_tag_astro_flow, desktop_latest_post and desktop_about_regression protect the existing reading surfaces and carry the Reading room in the footer.
desktop_footer_home and mobile_footer_home scroll the Reading room into view and must show the ivory/indigo strip without horizontal overflow.
desktop_footer_about protects the strip's presence on the About page footer.
desktop_theme_toggle clicks the theme button; the 'Room light' readout must then read 'lamplight'.
mobile_menu_open clicks the mobile menu control; its aria-expanded state must flip.

change_completion: The Reading room strip is present in the footer of the home, blog, About and tag pages (the shared component reaches all four routes).
After clicking the theme toggle on the home page, the 'Room light' readout updates to 'lamplight' (dark) — the post-interaction terminal state changed from 'daylight'.
design_consistency: The strip on the footer states matches the reference's ivory/indigo editorial styling under the visual-regression gate (pixel/ssim/block-fidelity), not an off-palette slab.
The strip adopts the blog's palette and a dashed-tag idiom so it reads as part of the site across light and dark.
responsive: No captured reading surface overflows horizontally beyond 24px on a 390px phone; the chip row wraps.
desktop_footer_home, mobile_footer_home and desktop_footer_about keep the Reading room strip readable across viewports without clipping or overflow.
regression: Navigation (Home/About/Blog/Tags), the footer, the mobile menu and light/dark theming remain present and functional.
The existing post/tag content, tag routing, RSS and the Astro build are not removed or broken, with no console or network errors.

metadata.design_goal: add a shared, theme-aware footer strip across every reading surface while keeping the theme, navigation and build stable
metadata.source_repo_kind: Astro editorial blog with shared Header/Footer, light/dark theme toggle, mobile menu, homepage, blog index, article routes, tag index/detail routes and an About page

author_notes: slot_266 L4 hardening of the withastro blog-tutorial-demo Astro editorial blog. The full tutorial-blog content is shared byte-identically across legs; the L4 levers ride on a new shared 'Reading room' footer strip. reference = strip on all pages, fluid wrap, ivory/indigo styling, theme-synced readout (passes D2/D3/D4/D6). baseline = the original unrepaired strip: present on home only (fails D2 cross-page), fixed 720px nowrap (fails D6 mobile overflow), plain gray slab (fails D3), but its readout IS theme-synced (passes D4). bad = a 'smart wrong' strip: present on home+blog only (fails D2 about/tags), 560px nowrap + overflow-x:hidden shallow non-fix (fails D6), off-palette dark-teal slab (fails D3), and the theme toggle flips the .dark class but the readout stays 'daylight' (fails D4) — bad fails 4 orthogonal gates. Design keywords: layout, palette, responsive, visual, interaction, editorial.
